messages:
Cara: FYI customer sent a 3.1MB payload in the POC and got a 413. They included a 120k-word legal addendum in one message :grimacing:
Pranav: Ugh. Which endpoint are they hitting? chat or embeddings?
Cara: chat.generate via our hosted API, model redwood-qa-open-16k. They said it failed at the start of the session when uploading conversation history. Error: 413 Request Entity Too Large.
Eli: Are they sending UTF-16 by any chance? That can double byte sizes.
Cara: I asked — they said they copied from MS Word, not sure of encoding. They pasted plain JSON in the request body.
Olga: Quick repro needed. Can someone ask for the exact `Content-Length` and a snippet of the request? Also, is the gateway returning nginx or our app-level 413?
InfraBot: deploy-prod-gw: upstream returned 413 from backend. raw_log: "client 10.4.5.6: payload too large"
Pranav: Ok gateway-level. We have a 2MB body limit on the public ingress for hosted customers. For this POC we can suggest: 1) chunking conversation history, 2) presigned upload + pass URL, or 3) use streaming + append context server-side.
Cara: Customer asks for presign option — they can't change client to do chunking quickly. Any docs or quick presign example I can forward?
Eli: Send them this pattern: upload the long blob to S3 (or their object store) and pass a short metadata pointer in the chat request. We support `context_url` pattern on Dedicated/Private — for hosted POC we can issue a temporary presign via our ingestion helper. Example snippet: `{"context_url":"https://s3.amazonaws.com/.../presigned?X-Amz-...","context_size":3172864}`
Olga: Note: security team asked about data residency for presigned uploads. For enterprise, recommend Dedicated or Private to keep blobs in their VPC.
Cara: They're also asking about pricing — will presigned uploads affect token billing?
Pranav: Only the tokens that get fed into the model count. If you do server-side chunking + summarization before sending, fewer tokens. If customer stores raw context externally and we fetch on-demand, be careful: fetching+processing still generates tokens. Presigned upload itself doesn't incur token cost.
Cara: Customer is on a tight timeline — wants a quick workaround to demo tomorrow. Any minimal change client-side?
Eli: Quick workaround: gzip the JSON body and set `Content-Encoding: gzip` if their client accepts it — reduces size ~70% for text. But many browsers and SDKs need explicit support. Also ensure API gateway allows `Content-Encoding`.
Pranav: If they can't gzip, do naive chunking: split the conversation into N messages and call the API multiple times, aggregating responses. For chat continuity, you can keep an internal condensed history: `system: previous convo summary` then append last 2 messages verbatim.
Cara: I'll relay both options (presign + small helper snippet, and gzip hint) and ask for `Content-Length`. Also mention Dedicated for long-term.
Olga: I can flag this in the security questionnaire: presigned flow requires object-store audit logs and a short retention TTL. That should unblock Security for a demo presign.
Cara: Thanks. One more ask — can Infra increase hosted ingress limit for a POC?
Pranav: We can temporarily increase the gateway body limit for their account but need EngOps approval (and it's not ideal for production). Ping @Eli with account ID and I'll route an exception if they really need it for the demo.
Eli: Got it. Cara — send account ID and a short justification. I'll queue the exception.
Cara: Sending details now. Appreciate it :thumbsup:
Pranav: Follow-up: remind them about sequence-length (model token max). Even if the body uploads, the model may truncate to 16k tokens. Suggest semantic chunking + retrieval approach for very long docs.
Cara: Noted. I'll include that in the email. Thanks team.
